confidence_notes: I ran two web searches. The first was for the RBA rate. A third-party summary gave 0.6720 USD per AUD at 4 pm AEST on 18 Nov 2026 and cited the RBA's exchange-rates page, but I did not open that page myself. The second search was one cost-of-living search for Interlaken. Results summarised Citycost, Whereandwhen and a Numbeo-based travel guide, but I did not open the pages, and the sources date from 2023 to 2026 and mix currencies. Coffee (about CHF 4.8–5) and restaurant meals are the best supported: an inexpensive meal is about CHF 24–25, and a mid-range three-course dinner for two is about CHF 116–120. The beer figure is a draft beer in a restaurant, priced from general Swiss knowledge at about CHF 7–8. The sources only gave supermarket bottle prices for beer, so I did not use them. Cocktails (about CHF 17–18) and wine by the glass (about CHF 8–9) are less certain. I estimated them from what I know about prices in Swiss tourist towns and how they usually compare with beer. All accommodation figures are my own estimates for peak July season and were not checked against live listings. Interlaken's summer demand pushes hotel and hostel prices well above Swiss averages, so those figures are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Treated as a high-cost Swiss alpine tourist town, comparable to Lucerne, Grindelwald and Zermatt. Food and drink prices are close to Zurich or Bern levels. Peak-season accommodation is priced at a premium because of tourism demand. I used roughly 1.24 USD per CHF to estimate the USD anchors.
